severity_notes:
- An acked `Durable` record that is not on disk, or does not replay after a crash, is severe. So is anything that lets two daemons own one `wab_dir`.
- A change to the on-disk WAB format, the wire protocol or a published crate's public API without a version decision is severe: it needs the owner (semver, the `docs_drift` guards).
- A panic reachable from a client frame, a stored segment or a config value is critical.
- A secret (sink URL credentials, bearer token, crates.io token) reaching a log, a `Debug` string, argv or `/status` is critical.
- Anything that loosens a security default (peer UID check, socket permissions, mTLS on TCP) is severe, and is never fixed overnight without the owner.

Scope of this epic (from its spec, docs/superpowers/temper/cleanup-2026-11/spec.md): the whole repository at the branch tip, NOT only `git diff main...epic/cleanup-2026-11` (the branch starts equal to main, so that diff is just the spec). Review the code itself, in your lens's area (the spec's Scope table). A finding needs an input and a wrong result that a verifier can reproduce; style, refactors and perf ideas are not findings.
These are owner items (kind owner), never fixes: a change to the WAB or `.confirmed` format, the wire protocol, `--json` shapes or a published crate's public API; loosening a security default; a new or upgraded dependency; D10 (explicit missing --config only WARNs: a deferred owner decision).
build_rule:
Every build, test, clippy or gate on beast runs as a jobq job: never run cargo, a gate script or a test binary directly in your ssh session (beast's ~/agents/CLAUDE.md; a session that compiled outside jobq was OOM-killed). Work in a worktree under ~/work/weir/ on beast; jobq's --cwd is that worktree's physical path (`pwd -P`).

Submit, then wait in the foreground (a single Bash call must stay under 10 minutes, so never use `jobq run` for a gate, and never end your turn while a job of yours is queued or running):
  ssh beast 'cd <worktree> && JOBQ_SUBMITTER=temper-cleanup ~/.local/bin/jobq submit --profile rust --project weir --cores 4 --mem 4G --timeout 3h --cwd "$(pwd -P)" --name <your-label>-quick -- bash .temper/gate-quick.sh'
  ssh beast '~/.local/bin/jobq wait <id>'   (call it again, with a Bash timeout of 600000 ms, until the job ends; its exit status is the gate's)
The full gate is the same with `--mem 8G --timeout 5h --name <your-label>-full -- bash .temper/gate-full.sh`. One cargo command (a reproduction, a single test) is the same with `--mem 4G --timeout 1h --name <your-label>-run -- bash .temper/gate-run.sh <cargo args>`, e.g. `... -- bash .temper/gate-run.sh test -p weir-wab segment`.
A job's env is cleared: pass variables as `-- env VAR=value bash .temper/gate-run.sh ...`. Read results from `~/.local/bin/jobq logs <id> --tail 400` (it prints only the last 200 lines by default) and from the gate's summary, /srv/bulk/Projects/weir/logs/gate/<worktree dir name>/latest-<quick|full|run>/summary.txt, whose last line is `GATE <name> rc=N`. A job's peak memory includes page cache: if a job is OOM-killed, resubmit once with a 2G larger --mem and say so in your result. Never cancel or touch another submitter's jobs. Keep at most one job of yours queued or running at a time. Beast's rule is at most 4 builds of this run at once: before each submit, run `ssh beast 'JOBQ_SUBMITTER=temper-cleanup ~/.local/bin/jobq list --mine | grep -cE " (queued|running) "'`; while it prints 4 or more, wait with `ssh beast 'sleep 120'` and check again.
Never set CARGO_TARGET_DIR or make another target dir: the gate slots are the build dirs; a gate that waits for a slot or for jobq's memory is normal. Never run sudo, never run the chaos harness's power-cut campaign, never touch docker images, volumes or containers that aren't weir's, never write the CI-skip token in a commit message. Commits carry only the `Temper-Task` trailer: no Co-Authored-By, Claude-Session or "Generated with" lines. Never print a secret or token.
A fix also adds one line under CHANGELOG.md `## [Unreleased]` (replace its "Nothing yet." line), in `### Fixed`, or `### Changed` for a behaviour an operator can notice, in the file's existing style. The `docs_drift` and `demo_drift` tests guard figures and version strings in the docs: if a fix trips one, fix the doc, never weaken the guard.
Clean up what you start on beast (test processes, tmux servers); leave worktrees in place.

selected.summary: The security-r3-01 fix (9c7b33e) limits the HTTP sink to scheme://host[:port] on its Debug, transport, health and startup paths, but the 3xx path still interpolates the response's Location header in full. An HTTP-to-HTTPS redirect echoes the configured webhook path, so the path secret reaches the WARN log, the dead-letter reason and the admin /status text. configuration.md and container.md now say a path token 'is never printed'.
selected.input: sink_type=http, sink_url=http://hooks.example.com/services/T0/B0/PATHSECRETTOKEN, and an endpoint that answers '301 Moved Permanently' with 'Location: https://hooks.example.com/services/T0/B0/PATHSECRETTOKEN' (a standard http-to-https upgrade). Reproduced on beast with a temporary probe test against the existing spawn_mock_server (jq-01M6YF1VEK827Z6ZGC9JSE8MWV); the probe edits were reverted afterwards.
selected.wrong_result: The dead-letter reason is "http 301 Moved Permanently: unexpected redirect to 'https://hooks.example.com/services/T0/B0/PATHSECRETTOKEN'; redirects are not followed ...". The same text goes to the warn! line in commit_per_record and commit_ndjson. sanitize_admin_text (redact_url_password) leaves it unchanged for /status, because it scrubs only userinfo and the 10 denylisted query keys. Fix: report only url_origin(location). Also reported by sinks-r4-01, which adds: a downstream 4xx body that echoes the request path (Express's default `Cannot POST /services/.../SECRET`) leaks it the same way through body_excerpt.

selected.summary: The ClickHouse query-password fix (126e8a3) redacts only the commit and health transport errors. ClickHouseSink::new's non-http-scheme error still prints base_url verbatim, and split_credentials leaves a ?password= query in base_url, so the password reaches the startup error on stderr.
selected.input: sink_type=clickhouse with a native-protocol / clickhouse-go style DSN, e.g. sink_url=tcp://127.0.0.1:9000?username=default&password=QPSECRET. Reproduced on beast with a temporary probe unit test (jq-01M6YF1VEK827Z6ZGC9JSE8MWV, --features clickhouse-sink); the probe edits were reverted afterwards.
selected.wrong_result: ClickHouseSink::new returns "clickhouse sink: url is not a valid http(s) URL: scheme 'tcp' is not http or https (in tcp://127.0.0.1:9000?username=default&password=QPSECRET)". select.rs wraps that error as 'failed to build ClickHouse sink: ...', and main returns it with ?, so the password is printed to stderr / the journal. Fix: run base_url through sql_common::redact_password (or url_origin) in that arm, the same as the parse-error arm.

selected.summary: RecordId hashes only `shard_NN/seg_NNNNNNNN.wab.sealed` + index + payload, and segment counters restart at seg_00000001 once a shard drains empty and the daemon restarts (or a pod without its PVC is redeployed), so a byte-identical record after the restart gets the RecordId of one already delivered (sinks-r4-02).
selected.input: Heartbeat producer `{"status":"ok"}` with sink_http_batch = "none" (or Postgres/MySQL with sink_*_id_column set). The drain confirms and deletes every segment, the daemon restarts on the same wab_dir, and the first heartbeat is pushed again. Reproduced on beast (jq-01M6YEYRPCYH6ECMW9HWF3XJPQ): both lives produced shard_00/seg_00000001.wab.sealed and the same RecordId f309d9ea...1dba3.
selected.wrong_result: The acked post-restart record gets the same per-record Idempotency-Key / id_column value as a delivered record; Postgres/MySQL ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING / INSERT IGNORE drops it permanently, an idempotent HTTP endpoint replays its cached 2xx, and weir confirms and deletes the segment: silent loss of acked records.

selected.summary: The lost+found fix (f7efcc9, f1a1e0d) made recovery, replay and attest look only at shard_<N> directories. compute_wab_bytes_on_disk still treats every directory except dead_letter and quarantine as a shard, so an unreadable foreign directory fails every WAB size scan, and with wab_max_bytes set the daemon refuses every push for good.
selected.input: wab_dir at a filesystem mount root, holding a root-owned lost+found the daemon user cannot read (reproduced on beast as a mode-000 directory beside shard_00 holding a 100-byte segment), and wab_max_bytes set (1,000,000 in the probe).
selected.wrong_result: compute_wab_bytes_on_disk returns None instead of Some(100). startup_cap_gate then sets wab_cap_rejecting to true (the fail-closed path), and every 5 s poll scan fails the same way, so the flag never clears. Every Push and PushBatch gets Nack(InternalError, cause wab_cap), /readyz stays 503 wab_cap_rejecting, and weir_wab_bytes_on_disk never updates. The fix in 2ad211a (judge the size afresh on the first scan that succeeds) cannot help, because no scan ever succeeds. Startup now gets past this exact input, so the daemon starts but accepts nothing. Probe (a temporary test, since reverted; the worktree is clean): jq-01M6YEYN6ED0EDQ19E4S8TVJR7 printed `PROBE readable=false bytes=None gate=None rejecting=true`. The fix is to filter with shard_id_from_path, the same rule as recovery, replay and scan_wab_lag.

selected.summary: The first push clears the fail-closed WAB-cap flag that a failed startup scan sets: over_wab_cap runs cap::evaluate with wab_bytes_now still at its initial 0, which is below low water. Pushes are admitted before any scan has succeeded, and the CHANGELOG entry for 2ad211a claims the opposite.
selected.input: Set wab_max_bytes (say 1000) and let startup_cap_gate's compute_wab_bytes_on_disk fail. On this branch that happens with an unreadable lost+found in wab_dir: recovery now skips it and startup proceeds, but the size scan still fails on it. A dirent error does the same. The WAB on disk is already over the cap. Then a producer sends one Push or PushBatch. Reproduced on beast (jq-01M6YFTGEAVVK5TS0W597TE25N) with a probe test: startup_cap_gate(missing_dir, 1000, ..), then cap::evaluate(1000, board.wab_bytes_now, &board.wab_cap_rejecting), which is exactly what over_wab_cap does. It printed `R4PROBE bytes_now=0 refused=false flag_after=false`.
selected.wrong_result: The push is acked and wab_cap_rejecting is set to false. /readyz stops reporting wab_cap_rejecting, so the 'pushes nack (fail-closed) until a scan succeeds' guarantee (spec §6 step 9 and the WARN in startup_cap_gate) is broken by the first record. If every later scan also fails (the lost+found case), wab_bytes_now stays 0 and the cap never rejects again, so the WAB grows without bound. The new CHANGELOG 'Fixed' entry says the placeholder 'kept pushes nacked ... for good', which disagrees with the code: the push path releases it at once.

selected.summary: The published sink-SDK docs and integrating.md still say the content-only DedupToken is fine where a duplicate is cheap (an archive, a log, an analytics table). This epic dropped that key from both built-in sinks because it makes downstreams drop distinct batches, and the DedupToken Stability note (lib.rs:376-377) still says upgrading keeps deduplicating.
selected.input: A third-party sink author follows the crate docs ('SinkBatch::dedup_token ... Fine for an archive') or docs/getting-started/integrating.md:294 ('A duplicate is cheap ... dedup_token() is simpler'). They send the token as a ClickHouse-style block or idempotency key. The producer pushes the same heartbeat every 30 s, so each timed-seal segment drains as a byte-identical one-record batch.
selected.wrong_result: Every such batch carries the same token. The downstream keeps the first and silently drops the rest while weir confirms and deletes them, so acked records are lost. This is the sinks-r3-01/-02 defect, which the docs present as only a duplicate risk when sink_max_batch_size changes. The Stability paragraph also says the 1.x-identical digest means 'an operator upgrading mid-outage keeps deduplicating'. The ClickHouse sink no longer sends it, and the CHANGELOG says an in-flight batch is re-sent once.

selected.summary: The crossed-reply fix (4b99f49) rejects the pending request only on the Ack and HealthCheckResponse branches. The AckTracked-for-untracked branch and the default unknown-type branch shift the pending entry off the queue and then call fail() without rejecting it, so the promise never settles, and timeoutMs cannot settle it either.
selected.input: A peer answers push('x') (or healthCheck()) with a well-formed AckTracked frame, or with any unknown message_type such as 0x7f, on a client made with timeoutMs: 1000. Reproduced with a local node script against the branch's client.ts.
selected.wrong_result: The push() promise stays pending forever. The script printed 'Push answered with AckTracked: STILL PENDING after 3000ms (timeoutMs=1000)' and the same for 0x7f. The timeout timer only calls fail(), and onClose rejects only entries still in the queue, so the caller hangs. That contradicts the CHANGELOG entry saying a reply of the wrong kind is now treated as a desync. desync_crossed_reply.ts does not test either case.

selected.summary: sigterm_unlinks_the_socket_at_once_and_metrics_stay_up_until_exit connects an idle client and sends SIGTERM without waiting for the daemon to accept that connection; if the listener closes first, Linux resets the never-accepted connection (ECONNRESET) and the test's EOF assertion fails. Decision Q5 promises EOF only for accepted idle connections. It failed once in a quick gate (jq-01M6V6SJAE0K2G3Z0SZHZQQRJJ).
selected.input: A loaded machine, so SIGTERM is handled before the daemon's accept loop picks up the test's idle connection.
selected.wrong_result: The client's read returns ECONNRESET instead of EOF, and the test fails though the daemon kept its documented contract.

answers.recordid-segment-instance: Owner, 8 Nov: fix this in PR #77, server-side; an approved contract change. Contract: (1) weir-server's segment identity, the string passed as `segment` to weir_sink_sdk::RecordId::for_record (drain/mod.rs segment_identity and every other caller that derives a RecordId for a record being delivered, dead-lettered or requeued), becomes `<shard_NN>/<segment file name>@<created_at as 16 lowercase hex digits>`, where created_at is the segment header's creation time in unix nanoseconds, the same value SinkBatch::segment_created_at and the S3 key use. (2) No change to weir-sink-sdk's API or to RecordId::for_record itself. (3) The identity stays stable across replays of the same segment instance (same file, same header), and differs across a restart that reuses a segment name. (4) Tests: the existing segment_identity tests updated to the new form; a new test that two segment instances with the same name and different created_at give different RecordIds for a byte-identical record at the same index, while re-reading the same segment gives the same ids. Update tests that pin RecordId values only where they pin the identity string, and say which ones in your note. (5) CHANGELOG `### Changed`: every RecordId value changes once at upgrade, so per-record HTTP Idempotency-Keys, Postgres/MySQL id_column values, S3 object names and the ClickHouse/NDJSON batch keys (which include the first RecordId) differ for records delivered after the upgrade; a record in flight at the upgrade is re-sent once under its new id (an id_column table may hold it twice, once). Update the docs that describe how RecordId is derived (docs/sinks/, configuration.md, the SDK's RecordId docs if they describe the segment argument as the file name).
answers.sigterm-test-accept-race: Head, 8 Nov (owner asked to close the flake): don't loosen the assertion. Make the test certain the idle connection is accepted before SIGTERM, e.g. one HealthCheck round-trip on that same connection, then leave it idle and send SIGTERM, and keep asserting EOF. No sleeps, no retries. The failing-test-first step can't reproduce the race on demand (150 isolated runs passed, jq-01M6Y7HWW24SZ0V32S3009NYYC): say so in your note and in the test comment, citing Q5.
